scope: Actual public browser with the existing bootstrap administrator session. Operator-assisted customer experience, not customer-scoped authorization or unaided onboarding. No control mutations or scientific submissions.

independent_rating.scale: Subjective 1-10 experience rating, not an SLA, scientific-quality assessment or statistically calibrated score.
independent_rating.interactive_api_basis: 70 of 71 exact synthetic Qwen outputs passed across HTTP/MCP, no client retries, short observed latencies and three successful recovery probes. One server-side MCP tool failure prevents an uninterrupted-availability claim.
independent_rating.scientific_unattended_batch_basis: The companion workload lane completed 13 of 14 operations and RF recovered two preempted attempts automatically. One impossible BindCraft CPU/flavor fit required operator diagnosis and cancellation; its UI gave no actionable error.
independent_rating.admin_operator_ui_basis: Model visibility, run detail and observability navigation are useful, but missing artifact-download action, misleading immutable-result freshness, unavailable per-run GPU totals and unhelpful placement/progress summaries impede customer work.
independent_rating.verdict: Suitable only for an operator-assisted pilot with known inputs and API result retrieval. Not ready for an unattended or unassisted customer batch trial until the scheduling, transient routability and result-access issues are fixed and tested.

completion.scientific_campaign_outcomes: 13 passed, one scheduler-blocked BindCraft explicitly cancelled; owned and reported by the independent workload lane.
completion.cleanup: Only this lane's sampler and browser processes were stopped; process lookup found neither remaining. All 70 returned Qwen operations were succeeded before recording PASS; the one failed MCP call returned no operation ID. No task GPU Pods, PVCs or scientific runs were created by this lane, and the existing Qwen serving Pod was retained.
completion.recovery_browser: At 15:21:25, full inventory showed 24 configured of 25 known (GLM excluded), Qwen hot 1/1, Cosmos intentionally cold 0/0 and scientific profiles batch-ready. This does not override the observed BindCraft placement failure under mixed load.

interactive_failure.server_correlation: Root's independent observer found Tool invoke_model unexpected exception at 15:12:03.426 in control-plane Pod pwmqv: RuntimeError that the registry model was not routable. MCP transport HTTP 200 at 15:12:03.429 does not mean the tool succeeded.
interactive_failure.cause_boundary: Server-side MCP tool failure is established. Why the route was unavailable is not yet established. The sampler discarded nested ExceptionGroup details, so the client record alone could not explain it.
interactive_failure.retry_policy: No client retry or replay; later independently scheduled HTTP and MCP requests passed. No claim of uninterrupted availability.

findings.observed: The BindCraft run and Design attempt say running and admitted on h100-1x, with 1 pod, node count unavailable, No error and No terminal error. No node_pending, Insufficient CPU, impossible resource fit or actionable recovery is displayed.
findings.independent_workload_diagnosis: The selected one-GPU pool cannot fit the Pod's 16.1 CPU request on 15.9 allocatable CPUs; scheduler/autoscaler evidence reports insufficient CPU and no scale-up/fallback. The workload owner explicitly cancelled only this test run at 15:12:46 after preserving the failure; it is not a successful unattended operation.
findings.recommendation: Correct resource-fit-aware placement or fallback for this existing model, and project the actual unschedulable reason and duration into the run UI. Do not treat Kueue admission alone as running computation.

findings.observed: RF's four independent attempts are usefully visible as two running, one preempted/retryable and one queued. The aggregate Queue and priority section simultaneously says pending, shows an Admitted timestamp, and says the controller has not observed a Kueue admission event.
findings.qualification: This is a mixed-shard summary inconsistency, not proof that all four shards failed or that platform priority/preemption failed. Final workload outcomes are reported separately.
findings.recommendation: Summarize admission per shard, including queued/admitted/running/preempted counts, instead of applying one binary admission label to a partially admitted bulk run.

findings.observed: A detail page opened at 15:13:32 remained unchanged in a 15:17:32 snapshot, including its 15:13:31 Updated header and old running/queued attempts. The public operation had completed at 15:16:34. One fresh navigation at 15:17:47 displayed succeeded, semantic validation passed, four successful shard outcomes and two preserved preempted attempts followed by successful second attempts.
findings.qualification: The terminal result exists and refresh works. This finding is lack of observed automatic progress refresh, not a failed operation or inaccessible result API. Two server-side retries after preemption are distinct from zero client resubmissions.
findings.recommendation: Provide a clear refresh action or bounded automatic refresh while runs are nonterminal, retaining the observation timestamp.

findings.observed: RFdiffusion and Protenix succeeded with semantic validation passed, but both manifest rows show Access: Not available. The API projection says artifact.state=available and artifact.download.available=false, href=null.
findings.cause: The current admin adapter hardcodes no download action and instructs callers to use the authorized artifact endpoint. This is independent of the freshness warning; no artifact loss or authorization failure was observed.
findings.workaround: Use the existing public scientific result/artifact API with the customer's own scientific key. The workload lane verified those actual downloads; this lane verified MCP status/result documents without creating grants.
findings.recommendation: Wire a clear authorized artifact-download action into the existing result UI; keep current tenant/model access checks. No new authorization architecture is needed.

findings.observed: Refreshing a completed RF result once and opening a newer completed Protenix result both show Stale data: scientific-artifacts observation exceeded the freshness bound.
findings.cause: Artifact observation time is set to immutable result commit time, then evaluated by a live-source freshness bound. A newly fetched completed result is therefore mislabeled stale.
findings.recommendation: Keep result creation/commit time distinct from the current read observation time, or explicitly classify immutable terminal evidence rather than applying live-metric staleness semantics.

findings.observed: Completed RF and Protenix pages and the mixed-run ledger show allocated, active, idle and grace GPU cards as unavailable. Lower RF phase cards expose59.31s active-compute and2.24s allocated-idle; completed stage rows retain1GPU and pool names. The UI cannot currently provide a reconciled per-run customer GPU-time total.
findings.qualification: This finding concerns the displayed per-run accounting projection. It does not infer missing backend samples, convert CPU/phase durations into GPU-seconds, or claim billing-ready totals from allocation estimates.
findings.recommendation: Join the actual allocation/release and active/idle lifecycle evidence into the existing run summary, with uncertainty and GPU multiplicity retained. Root's independent observer owns the accounting diagnosis.

findings.observed: Scientific runs → Scientific model catalog says Checkpoint unavailable · GPU snapshot unavailable for ESMFold2/Fast, Protenix and RF, while Full model inventory correctly says Available as an option for their installed qualified bundles.
findings.qualification: A normal-loaded run saying restore not-observed is truthful and not a bug. The inconsistency is a model-level capability display using the same unavailable wording for absence of a per-run observation.
findings.recommendation: Separate qualified/selectable capability, configured preference and observed execution backend in model-level copy. Do not mark a normal-loaded run as restored.

findings.observed: Capacity & queues exposes Kueue resource quotas, admitted/pending workloads, reserved16GPU capacity and a preemptible pool that appeared during the campaign. An early Node scaler capability card said Healthy: No despite available adapter data; GPU Healthy values were unavailable without explicit health evidence.
findings.qualification: No claim that node scaling failed: a real scientific job used the preemptible pool and completed. Healthy GPU count, configured pool health and successful scheduling are separate facts.
findings.recommendation: Explain the exact unhealthy pool/bound condition in the operator card instead of a generic fleet-level message, and keep lack of health telemetry distinct from unhealthy hardware.

positive_observations: Consistent navigation/layout; the scientific ledger links directly to detailed run pages with tenant/key-prefix attribution, effective service class, stage DAG and statuses, timestamps, retries and semantic validation.
Actual mixed-run progress was visible: completed RF/Protenix/Mosaic and concurrent BoltzGen/BindCraft/Proteina/ESMFold2 stages, without relying on hidden Kubernetes inspection to find their UI state.
Full inventory distinguishes hot serving replicas, intentionally cold Cosmos and dispatchable scientific profiles; it explains snapshot option qualification separately from current execution.

The operation's observability link preserves the selected operation and exposes healthy Grafana/Loki/Tempo/Prometheus/DCGM/OTel/Kueue/KEDA tools. This lane did not establish that every external dashboard view automatically opens the intended query.

Existing academic credentials successfully discover all10 scientific profiles and read canonical completed RF/Protenix status/results through MCP. This is five read-only MCP calls, not an all-model MCP submission campaign.
harness_errors_not_platform_failures: r01 periodic /healthz requests returned404 because that route is not published; r02 uses verified /readyz. One-time /livez route discovery also returned404.
One manual Protenix URL contained an incorrect UUID and produced two frontend404 responses; the exact receipt-derived operation URL worked. The incorrect-attempt screenshot/record is retained.
Initial unauthenticated admin session lookup401 is expected; successful sign-in used an existing operator credential entirely in memory.
Playwright CLI could not read local credentials in its VM; the existing Node Playwright pattern was used with an in-memory session, without writing credentials or browser storage state.
